thread:
incident_bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: serving-runtime pod crashloop on node g12-az1 — repeated OOMs followed by CUDA illegal memory access (misaligned device address). Auto-escalating to #incidents.

alice.oncall: seeing surge of 5xx from the serving tier. p95/p99 latency spiking. customers: 2 Dedicated clusters on g12-az1.

ben.sre: I pulled the pod logs and kube events. root cause looks like repeated eviction -> reload -> illegal device addr during reload. quick snippets: 
```
kubectl logs -n serving svc-llm-frontend-7f8d9
E tensorflow_runtime: CUDA error: illegal memory access
E runtime: misaligned device address 0x7f8a3c000 (expected alignment 0x1000)
kernel: [ 1234.567890] gpu0: deviceaddr=0x7f8a3c000 unaligned access, terminating context
```

charu.runtime: copying raw nvcrash and dmesg to /tmp/incident-528600. please collect `dmesg | tail -n 200` and `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` from the node.

dave.infra: I've cordoned g12-az1 to stop new pods landing: `kubectl cordon g12-az1` and started draining non-critical pods. marking in progress.

alice.oncall: ETA on a replacement node? we need minimal customer impact. Maria, can you draft status page text?

maria.prod: drafting: "We are investigating an infrastructure issue affecting inference latency and errors for a subset of customers in us-west. Mitigation in progress: node cordon, traffic routed to fallback pool. We will update in 30 minutes."

charu.runtime: quick mitigation plan:
- scale replicas down to allow KV cache warmup on healthy nodes: `kubectl scale --replicas=4 deployment/serving-frontend`
- enable CPU fallback variant for heavy models: `redwoodctl route set --model v2-large --fallback v2-large-cpu`
- avoid live reloads: `kubectl annotate deployment/serving-frontend pause-reload=true`
Do these and we'll monitor error rate.

ben.sre: executed the scale and fallback. error rate dropped from 3.7% -> 1.2% over last 4 minutes. p99 latency still elevated because a few in-flight requests retried.

alice.oncall: good. collecting evidence for postmortem. charu, can runtime grab the coredump and kernel trace? we need to determine if this is an in-kernel race or a driver/kernel incompat.

charu.runtime: on it. I requested nv-support dump: `sudo /usr/local/bin/nvcrash --collect --output /tmp/nvcrash-528600.tar.gz`. also grabbed `perf top` and `gdb` backtraces from the serving process. attaching trimmed stack: 
```
#0  0x7f9b2a1c in memcpy_fromio
#1  0x7fae4cc0 in gpu_kv_cache_restore
#2  0x7fac1010 in serving_reload_handler
#3  0x55f4b2 in main_loop
```
Looks like KV cache restore touches an unaligned GPU pointer when the process is restarted during eviction. Possible race between eviction path and cache restore.

dave.infra: node g12-az1 has had 2 OOM kills in the last 24h for other workloads (syslog shows memory pressure). I'm scheduling a proactive replace of g12-az1; creating a new node pool with same instance type and migrating workloads.

ben.sre: note — recent kernel update applied 6 hours ago on g12-az1 (linux-5.15.92 -> 5.15.94). driver nv 525.85.12. we should verify driver/kernel compat. adding to the checklist for eng-runtime.

alice.oncall: customer impact: two Dedicated customers (acct A123, B987) will have degraded availability (retries/latency). We routed traffic to fallback but there will be transient errors for inflight requests. Maria, add that to status update.

maria.prod: updated status page: "Mitigation: traffic rerouted to fallback pool; cordoned node; reduced replicas. Impact: partial errors for small subset of requests; customers A123 and B987 may see retries. Next update in 30m or on status change." :white_check_mark:

charu.runtime: triage decision: reproduce locally using rapid eviction + reload loop. if reproducible, prepare a small runtime patch to guard alignment in KV restore (align with `cudaHostRegister`/page-align check) and add a retry/backoff on restore. assigning to @charu.runtime to get a PR ready.

ben.sre: for immediate protection, I added an admission webhook rule: reject pods with `restartOnEvict=true` on nodes with kernel 5.15.94 and driver 525.85.12. This will reduce reload storm while we patch.

alice.oncall: good short-term. Escalation: charu, please pair with kernel eng if repro indicates kernel race. We might need a hotfix kernel rollback on the node pool.

charu.runtime: assigning to `eng-runtime` - tagging `@kernel-team` and `@drivers`. collecting repro artifacts: 1) nvcrash tarball 2) container core 3) dmesg 4) `kubectl describe pod`. Link: https://redwood.internal/incident/528600/artifacts

dave.infra: replacement nodes are up in pool g12-az1-b. I'm migrating pods off g12-az1 now. expected zero-customer-downtime for new pods.

ben.sre: monitoring: error rate steady at ~0.9%, p99 latency trending down. no new OOMs on other nodes.

alice.oncall: preparing handoff to night oncall in 45m. I'll include runbook and checkpoints:
- ensure g12-az1 remains cordoned until kernel/driver compatibility confirmed
- keep fallback enabled for heavy models
- watch error rate and p99 latency; escalate if error >2% or repeat OOM on another node
- collect all artifacts and link them into ticket ENG-528600

charu.runtime: I will open ENG-528600 with reproducer steps and attach nvcrash dump. initial hypothesis: misaligned device pointer during KV cache restore triggered by eviction race. priority P1 for runtime and kernel teams.

maria.prod: preparing customer follow-up templates and a post-incident email draft for A123/B987 with mitigation steps and ETA for fix.

deploybot: deployment rollback recorded: `serving-runtime@deploy-2026-03-02T18:12:43` -> rolled back to `deploy-2026-03-01T21:04:10` (requested by alice.oncall).

alice.oncall: handing off to ben.sre for overnight watch. Ben, please maintain watch for 3 hours and update channel if error >2% or node flaps. I'll be on call for escalation.

ben.sre: acknowledged. I'll keep an eye and will ping if anything changes. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

incident_bot: Incident 528600 marked "mitigated" — monitoring continues.

alice.oncall: thanks everyone — nice containment and thorough artifact collection. We'll follow up with a postmortem and an action item list (kernel rollback plan, runtime alignment guard, node pool replacement).
